extracted.intended_audience: early-career researchers/postdoctoral scientists interested in HFSP Postdoctoral Fellowships and the broader scientific community
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the eligibility, thematic priorities, and procedural/administrative requirements described for the Human Frontier Science Program (HFSP) Postdoctoral Fellowships (Long-Term and Cross-Disciplinary). Useful for prospective applicants and institutional advisers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research focus: novel, innovative, interdisciplinary basic research
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP supports novel, innovative and interdisciplinary basic research focused on the complex mechanisms of living organisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis placed on projects that are novel and innovative and that address complex biological mechanisms; priority for work at the frontier of the life sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on novel collaborations
rubrics_metrics.description: A clear emphasis is placed on novel collaborations that bring biologists together to focus on problems at the frontier of the life sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborations that are new or unusual and that unite biologists (potentially across subfields) to tackle frontier problems are favored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant career stage: postdoctoral/early-career
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdoctoral scientists (early-career) are the target awardees of HFSP Postdoctoral Fellowships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program is intended to foster the next generation of life science researchers; applicants should be at the postdoctoral stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — Long-Term Fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: Long-Term Fellowships are for applicants with a Ph.D. in a biological discipline who want to embark on a novel frontier project in life sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should hold a Ph.D. in a biological field and propose novel frontier basic research in the life sciences to be eligible for Long-Term Fellowships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — Cross-Disciplinary Fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-Disciplinary Fellowships are for applicants who hold a Ph.D. from outside of the life sciences (e.g., physics, chemistry, engineering, or computer science) but want to work on a novel frontier project in biology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants from non-life-science backgrounds proposing biology-focused frontier research are eligible under this category; interdisciplinary transition is a core feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: International mobility requirement (host lab location)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows are hosted by scientists in laboratories in a country that is different from where their Ph.D. was conferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful applicants must arrange a host laboratory in a different country than the one in which they obtained their Ph.D., reflecting HFSP's mobility requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship duration and financial support
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP Fellowships are three years in duration and provide support for the cost of living, and a research and travel allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards fund a three-year postdoctoral period and include living costs plus research and travel allowances; applicants should plan projects consistent with this duration and funding scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process and competitiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP Review Committee selects awardees from a large applicant pool; in 2026 HFSP reviewed proposals from 746 applicants, invited 126 to submit full proposals, and awarded 55 fellowships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is competitive and multi-stage (initial application -> invitation to submit full proposal -> final awards) judged by the HFSP Review Committee; applicants should expect rigorous peer selection and low award rates.
